Introduction1
CHAPTER
SECTION I: DATA COLLECTION TECHNIQUE
 Purpose of the Publication
 User Guide to Indian Police Statistics
• Statistics Covered
 Data source and quality
• Data Collection Tool
• Analytical Techniques
• Data Collection Procedure
 Data Limitations and Implications
• Conventions used
This section provides information regarding the purpose of publication, user guide
to Indian Police Statistics, data source and quality, statistical tools, the procedure of data
collection, limitations, and implications.
PURPOSE OF THE PUBLICATION:
The BPR&D has been publishing the “Data on Police Organizations” in India since
1986, annually. From time to time, some of the essential features like women police, police
expenditure, constabulary ratio, transport facilities, communication facilities, representation
of SCs/STs, and police training institutes were added.
```
In this publication, dimensions like the infrastructure of CAPFs (vehicle availability,
```
```
family quarters, training institutions, tracker and sniffer dogs, and pay scales), Gender- wise
```
data on Police Forces, District Armed Reserve Police, Senior Supervisory Officers, Immediate
Supervisory Officers, and Field Staff Ratio, Data of Women Police, Sanctioned and Actual
Strength of SCs/STs and OBCs have been added.
CHAPTER 1 - INTRODUCTION
36“PromotingGoodPracticesandStandards”
This issue of “Data on Police Organizations” in India, as on 01.01.2022, will be
more beneficial for the users, especially for the policymakers, police officers, researchers,
academicians, police administrators, and other stakeholders, as it is coming out timely.
DATA COLLECTION PROCEDURE:-
```
“Data on Police Organizations” in India (DoPO) has been prepared based on the data
```
provided by the States/UTs, CAPFs, and other Central Police Organizations. Further, data
```
have also been obtained from the Registrar General of India (RGI) and the Survey of India
```
```
(SOI).
```
STATISTICAL TOOLS:-
Statistical methods involved in carrying out the study include planning, designing,
collecting data, analyzing, drawing meaningful interpretation, and reporting the findings.
PRESENTATION OF DATA:-
Data are collected in a raw format. Therefore, data have been summarized, processed,
analyzed, and presented in charts and tables to make them more meaningful. However, in
this format, there are inherent difficulties in its understanding.
The graph is a very effective visual tool. It displays data at a glance, facilitates
comparison, reveals trends and relationships within the data, such as changes over time,
frequency distribution and correlation, etc. Bar graphs, Pie charts, and other statistical tools
have been used.
DATA LIMITATIONS:-
DoPO has been prepared based on data provided by the States/UTs/CAPFs and
other Police Organizations.
Police structures in different States/UTs, CAPFs, and CPOs are not uniform. In a few
```
cases, States/UTs have not provided complete data; consequently, it has been mentioned
```
```
as ‘Not Available (NA)/Not Provided (NP)’ in the relevant Tables and, at places. ‘0’ denotes
```
```
numeric value, whereas (-) denotes not available. Wherever appropriate, data of the previous
```
year has been incorporated for the sake of comparison.
CHAPTER 1 - INTRODUCTION
37“PromotingGoodPracticesandStandards”
SECTION II: INDIAN DEMOGRAPHY
 Male & Female Population
 Geographical Area
This section depicts the information/data of States/UTs regarding demography,
containing the country’s male-female population and geographical area.
MALE & FEMALE POPULATION
Demography is the statistical study of populations, especially human beings. At a
glance, it analyzes living population, i.e., changes over time and space in response to birth,
migration, aging, death, etc.
Its analysis covers entire society or groups defined by education, nationality, religion,
ethnicity, etc. Demographic studies also analyze the relationships between economic, social,
cultural, and biological processes influencing the population.
The total population of India, as on 01.10.2021, as provided by the Registrar General
of India and the Census Commissioner of India, is 137.03 crore, approx., comprising 70.43
crore males and 66.60 crore females.
Among the States, Uttar Pradesh, with a population of more than 23.23 Crore, is the
most populous state in the country, followed by Maharashtra, with a population of 12.50
crore.
Among the Union Territories, Delhi, with a population of more than 2.08 crore, is the
most populous UT in the country, followed by J&K, with a population of 1.34 crore.

terms of geographical area, the largest state in India is Rajasthan, with an area of 3,42,111
Sq. Km. and the smallest is the UT of Lakshadweep, with an area of 30 Sq. Km.

MODERNIZATION GRANTS TO THE STATE POLICE FORCES
Modernization grants to the state police forces, allocated by the MHA, are meant to
upgrade the infrastructure of the state police in order to improve their capacity to meet the
emerging challenges of internal security, besides improving efficiency and effectiveness in
Police service delivery.
The focus of the scheme is on strengthening of the police infrastructure by way of
construction of secure and people friendly Police Stations, Police Outposts, Police Housing,
improved Mobility, Modern Weaponry, Computerization, Communication Equipment, Modern
Traffic Control Equipment, etc.
At the national level, the grants made available to the state police forces in the financial
year 2021-22 by the Central Government and the State Governments and the total amount
utilized for modernization by the State Governments for the State Police Forces are given at

```
Data have been compiled about different types of transport facilities (vehicles)
```
available with the police force in the States/UTs Police and CAPFs. The number of vehicles
available per 100 police Personnel has also been calculated.
```
TRANSPORT FACILITIES (MOBILITY)
```
Mobility is measured in terms of the availability of vehicles to move the unit on the call
of duty. Police mobility is directly linked with its operational efficiency. During law and order
situations, the quick response of police forces helps significantly in protecting the life and
property of the people.
Vehicles required to provide mobility to Police Forces have been divided into four
```
categories, i.e., Heavy Vehicles (buses/trucks, troop carriers, etc.), Medium Vehicles, Light
```
```
Vehicles (jeeps/cars, etc.), and Very Light Vehicles (three/two Wheelers). Heavy, Medium
```
and Light vehicles cater to the requirements of the Police Stations and field-level supervisory
and senior supervisory officers.
Besides above, State Police have also procured some special purpose vehicles:
```
like Mines Protected Vehicles (MPV), Riot Control Vehicles, Ambulances, Mobile Forensic
```
Vans, Water Cannons, Water Tankers, Prison Vans, etc., to meet their specific needs. These
vehicles have been clubbed under the “ Other Category ”.
```
In all, 2,15,448 vehicles were available with State/UT Police Force in 2021; This
```
number increased from 2,07,030 during 2020. Out of 2,15,448 vehicles, 11,388 are Heavy-
duty Vehicles, 19,097 Medium-duty Vehicles, 89,386 Light Vehicles, 92,947 Very Light
```
Vehicles (two/three-wheelers) and 2,630 are Other Vehicles (Table No-5.1.6).
```

SECTION I: EQUIPMENT TO FACILITATE POLICING
 Computers, Servers & Laptops available

This section provides State/UT wise data on CCTV cameras, computers, servers and
laptops, speedometers, breath analyzers, and forensic science laboratories/mobile forensic
science vans available with the Police.
Police human resources alone are insufficient to curb crime, maintain law and order,
traffic management, internal security, and other policing requirements. Therefore, they must
be supplemented with modern facilities and gadgets like computers, CCTV cameras, traffic
and investigation equipment, speedometers, breath analyzers, forensic science kits/labs,
etc., to enhance effectiveness and efficiency.
```
FORENSIC SCIENCE LABORATORIES (FSLs)/MOBILE FORENSIC SCIENCE
```
```
VANS (MFSVs)
```
Data on forensic science laboratories/mobile forensic science vans have been
collected and compiled on 01.01.2022. At the national level, 690 Forensic Science
```
Laboratories (FSLs)/ MFSVs are available, out of which 32 are main laboratories, 106 are
```
```
regional laboratories, and the remaining 552 are mobile laboratories (Table No - 6.1.1).
```
COMPUTERS/SERVERS/LAPTOPS AVAILABLE
At the national level, 1,72,168 computers, 2,253 servers, and 18,741 laptops are
```
available with State/UT police as on 01.01.2022 (Table No - 6.1.2).
```

68“PromotingGoodPracticesandStandards”
NUMBER OF CAMERAS/CCTVS, SPEED GUNS, AND BREATH ANALYZERS
USED BY POLICE
The total number of 4,56,807 CCTV cameras, 2,970 speed guns, and 28,181 breath
```
analyzers are available with the State/UT Police as on 01.01.2022 (Table No - 6.1.3).
```
NUMBER OF SNIFFER AND TRACKER DOGS
At States/UTs level, 1,639 sniffers and 877 tracker dogs in all are available with the
Police, as on 01.01.2022. In the CAPFs, 1,753 sniffers and 463 tracker dogs are available, as
```
on 01.01.2022 (Table No - 6.1.4 and 6.1.5).
```
TERRORISM/EXTREMISM AFFECTED POLICE DISTRICTS
```
A total of 160 Police Districts are affected by terrorism or extremism (Appendix 5) as
```
provided by States/UTs.
The number of Police Districts affected by the terrorist/extremist problem during the
```
last nine years (2013-2021) shows a mixed trend. A slight decrease was noticed from 2013
```
to 2015, increasing from 2016-17 and decreasing in 2020 and again increased in 2021. It
may be seen from the graph given below.
CHAPTER 6 - OTHER DATA/INFORMATION
69“PromotingGoodPracticesandStandards”
```
CENTRAL ARMED POLICE FORCES (CAPFs) DEPLOYED IN THE STATES/
```
UTs
```
A total of 1,958 companies of Central Armed Police Forces (BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP,
```
```
SSB, etc.) were deployed on Internal Security duties in different States/UTs for more than six
```
```
months during 2021 (Table No - 6.1.7).
```
The deployment of the Central Armed Police Forces in the States/UTs had shown a
steady increase from 2013 to 2014 but has declined after that, as shown in the graph.
Further, through the analysis of the deployment of 1,958 companies of CAPFs, it is
observed that 701 companies of CAPFs were deployed in Jammu and Kashmir, followed
by 286 companies in Chhattisgarh. It indicates that the country’s North, Central, and North
Eastern regions, which are affected with Terrorism/Left Wing Extremism, Insurgency had a
significant deployment of CAPFs during the period.

70“PromotingGoodPracticesandStandards”
SECTION II: TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT
 Police Personnel Recruited
 Police Personnel Trained
 Information on IPS Officers
 State/UT Training Institutes
 CAPF/CPO Training Institutes
This section contains the data from States/UTs in respect of Police Personnel
```
(Constables and SIs) recruited during the year 2021 and the number of newly recruited
```
police personnel who underwent training.
POLICE PERSONNEL RECRUITED
The 45,438 Police Constables were recruited during 2021 against the 72,520 recruited
in 2020. At the State level, the highest number of 13,155 Constables were recruited in Bihar,
```
followed by 11,812 in Tamil Nadu (Table No - 6.1.8).
```
```
The number of Sub-Inspectors (SIs) recruited during 2021 was 6,694, whereas this
```
figure was 8,503 during 2020. At the State level, the highest number of SIs recruited were
```
2,218 in Bihar, followed by 968 in Tamil Nadu (Table No - 6.1.8).
```
TRAINING OF NEWLY RECRUITED POLICE PERSONNEL
```
Total 81,131 newly recruited Police Personnel from Constables to the Dy.SP (Civil,
```
```
District Armed Reserve, and Special Armed police) were trained during 2021 in State Police
```
Training Institutes. The break-up is 65,444 Constables, 5,629 Head Constables, 3,271 ASI,
```
6,125 SIs, 321 Dy.SP and 341 Any others (Table No - 6.1.10).
```
The highest number, i.e., 1,583 SIs, were trained by the Bihar Police, followed by
1078 SIs by Delhi. As far as Constables are concerned, 17,492 Constables were trained in
UP, followed by 13,203 from Telangana.
IPS OFFICERS
The sanctioned strength of IPS Officers, as on 01.01.2022, was 4,984 at the all- India
level, whereas 4,118 officers are available. Further, 458 IPS Officers were on deputation with
```
the Central Government (Table No - 6.2.2).
```
CHAPTER 6 - OTHER DATA/INFORMATION
71“PromotingGoodPracticesandStandards”
POLICE TRAINING INSTITUTES
Regular and adequate training of Police Personnel at all levels is necessary to upgrade
their professional knowledge, skills, and attitude and instill confidence and professionalism
in the Police Personnel. It contains information about Police Training Institutes of the States/
UTs and CAPFs. These institutions cater to the basic training of the newly recruited Police
Personnel, in-service training to Police Personnel of different ranks: specialized training
to the Police Personnel deployed for specialized work and assignments like Special Task
```
Force (STF), Special Investigation Teams (SITs), Commandos, etc. Some of these Training
```
Institutes have been recognized as the “Centre of Excellence” for imparting specialized
training in a particular field/ craft/ trade.
STATE TRAINING INSTITUTES
In 2021, 194 Training Institutes were being run by the State Police Forces. State-wise,
these institutes’ names, addresses, and contact numbers are given in Appendix-1. The
```
highest number of Training Institutes, i.e., twenty-four (24), is run by the Tamil Nadu Police,
```
followed by 18 by the Madhya Pradesh Police.
UT TRAINING INSTITUTES
In 2021, a total number of 17 Training Institutes were being run by the UT Police. The
```
highest number of Training Institutes, i.e., seven (7), were being run by the J&K Police. The
```
names, addresses, and contact numbers are given in Appendix-1.
CAPF/CPO TRAINING INSTITUTES
During 2021, a total number of 103 Training Institutes were being run by the Central
Armed Police Forces/Central Police Organizations, out of which 25 were run by the BSF,
```
followed by 22 by the CRPF (Appendix-2 & 6).
```

SECTION III: PPMG and PMG
 PPMG and PMG
 Pay Scales of Police Officers
This section provides State/UT wise data on Police Personnel awarded Gallantry
```
Medals (PPMG and PMG) and Pay Scales of Police Personnel in different States/UTs and
```
CAPFs.
PRESIDENT’S POLICE MEDAL/POLICE MEDAL FOR GALLANTRY
President’s Police Medal/Police Medals for Gallantry is awarded to Police Personnel to
execute the conspicuous act of gallantry in saving life and property or preventing crimes, or
```
arresting dangerous criminals. A total of 27 President’s Police Medals for Gallantry (PPMG)
```
```
and 869 Police Medals for Gallantry (PMG) were awarded for outstanding performance of
```
Police Personnel from States/UTs/CAPFs and CPOs. Out of 869 Police Medals for Gallantry
awarded in 2021, the highest number, 308 PMGs, was awarded to the Jammu and Kashmir
```
Police, followed by 218 to the CRPF (Table No - 6.2.5).
```
PAY SCALES OF POLICE OFFICERS
A comparative chart displaying Scales of Police Personnel from Constable to Dy.SP
among the different States/UTs/CAPFs/CPOs are given in Appendix - 3, 4, and 7.

Dial - 112
For all kinds of emergencies and distress calls a nationwide,
unified emergency response system with a single emergency
number ‘Dial-112’ is designed to provide assistance to the
people in distress within the best possible time after getting
distress signals from citizens in the form of voice call, SMS,
e-mail, panic SOS request, web request etc. Currently,
Helpline number Dial-100 has been merged in Dial-112. 101
```
(Fire and Rescue) and 108 (ambulance, 181 (women and
```
```
Child Care) etc. will also be integrated in this unified number
```
‘112’

Voice Call- Dial-112
Messaging- SMS to 112

Distress Web Requests - https://pb.ners.in Panic Messaging -
Mobile Panic Button App for citizens - 112 INDIA APP

helpline is a multi channel platform which can be accessed
